issues.legal_issue: A court conducting an execution sale must sell only the portion of attached property necessary to satisfy the decree when that portion can be separately sold, and a sale of the entire property without considering this requirement is invalid.
material_facts: The execution claim was about Rs. 2,400, while the attached land measured 10 acres and was sold for Rs. 17,000.
The land was not indivisible, and a portion could conveniently have been demarcated and sold.
The executing court did not consider whether selling only a portion would satisfy the execution claim.
issues.conclusion: The sale of the entire property was illegal and without jurisdiction and was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 64 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the executing court to determine whether the whole attached property or only a portion is necessary to satisfy the decree. This is an obligation, not merely a discretion; even a single property must be sold only in part where a separate portion can be sold lawfully and will suffice. A sale made without examining this requirement is illegal and without jurisdiction. The Court relied on Takkaseela Pedda Subba Reddy v. Pujari Padmavathamma & Ors., [1977] 3 SCC 337, which held that execution sales must stop once the decree is satisfied.

rule.if: execution_sale and claim_small_relative_to_property and property_portion_separately_saleable and court_failed_to_consider_sufficient_portion

predicates.execution_sale: A court conducted a sale of attached property to execute a decree.
predicates.claim_small_relative_to_property: The execution claim was small in relation to the value or extent of the property sold.
predicates.property_portion_separately_saleable: A portion of the property could be separately sold without violating the law, and division was not impracticable or undesirable.
predicates.court_failed_to_consider_sufficient_port: The court did not consider whether selling only a sufficient portion of the property would satisfy the execution claim.
predicates.execution_sale_is_invalid: The execution sale is illegal and must be set aside.

issues.definition: When a court sells property to execute a decree, and the claim is small relative to the property, a separately saleable portion exists, and the court fails to consider selling only a sufficient portion, the sale is invalid.
